exposure_measure: Endorsement that GOVERNMENT SHOULD DEAL WITH environmental problems
exposure_items_quoted: government should deal with environmental problems""
effect_value: lower average fertility desires; driven by decreased desire for LARGE families
notes: WALL 1 BLEED-IN, AND IT IS THE SAME MEASURE THAT ROUTED TRAYLOR & CHAE OUT OF THE REALIZED POOL. The exposure is a government-environmental-policy preference, not ecological fear, not habitability concern, and not eco-ethical concern about procreation. Under Wall 1 clause (a) this measures D.1.a's construct. Recommend routing to D.1.a on the same grounds and for the same reason; flagged rather than moved unilaterally because the gate is the RA's call. Counted as a bleed-in in the rate.

exposure_measure: Climate Change Awareness Scale (CCAS), 25 items in FIVE subscales
exposure_items_quoted: climate-friendly behavior, knowledge, personal concern, attitude, and multiplicative action
notes: MIXED MEASURE, PARTIAL BLEED-IN. Two of the five CCAS subscales -- climate-friendly BEHAVIOR and KNOWLEDGE -- are not fear content; personal concern and attitude are closer. A composite that averages behaviour with concern cannot be assigned cleanly to D.3.b, and the paper reports on the composite. Extraction of the subscale-level coefficients is required before this can be used, otherwise the chapter would import a partly-D.1.a construct.

estimand: climate change vs five other constraints -> childbearing intentions
exposure_measure: Factorial-survey vignette dimension: the pace of climate change, varied against employment stability, housing affordability, childcare availability, men's domestic contribution, and abortion rights
exposure_items_quoted: employment stability, housing affordability, childcare availability, men's share in childcare and housework, the pace of climate change, abortion rights
outcome: Intentions to have a first or second child
effect_value: climate concerns LESS INFLUENTIAL than economic security and reproductive autonomy
notes: THE STATED TRACK'S WALL 3 TEST, AND IT POINTS AGAINST D.3.b. This is a randomised vignette design that holds six constraints against each other in one instrument, so the comparison is internal rather than across studies. Authors: 'Results confirm the enduring salience of economic security for fertility intentions ... Climate concerns are less influential.' READ ALONGSIDE gol_05: Golovina's fully adjusted GSOEP models found climate worry significant where economic worry was not. Two within-study Wall 3 comparisons pointing OPPOSITE WAYS -- one on realized births in Germany, one on stated intentions in Poland. The chapter should report the conflict, not average it.

estimand: climate change worry -> intention to remain childless
exposure_measure: Climate change worry (very worried vs not/somewhat worried)
effect_value: more likely to intend to remain childless; less likely to intend to have children
notes: Positive finding on the EXTENSIVE margin, and the author notes it is the first representative-sample European evidence. Driven by the 18-24 and 25-34 age groups. Effect sizes not yet extracted from the body.

estimand: climate change worry -> total intended number of children
notes: NULL ON THE INTENSIVE MARGIN, in the same study and sample that finds an extensive-margin effect. 'there is no association between climate worries and the total intended number of children.' The margin distinction matters for TICK-052: an effect on whether to have any children and no effect on how many is a different demographic object from a uniform reduction in family size.

exposure_measure: Climate Anxiety Scale (Clayton & Karazsia), cognitive-emotional impairment + functional impairment subscales
exposure_items_quoted: CAS ... two subscales representing Cognitive-Emotional Impairment
outcome: Family planning, among four 'future planning' domains
design: Cross-sectional survey of environmental degree students
notes: NULL, AND INFORMATIVE BECAUSE THE SAMPLE IS THE MOST LIKELY PLACE TO FIND AN EFFECT. Quoting: 'we did not find that environmental degree students' concerns about climate change more strongly affected other life choices such as family planning, long-term habitation, financial decisions and travel plans.' Climate anxiety DID strongly affect career/future planning in the same study, so the null is specific to family planning rather than a failure of the exposure measure.

estimand: eco-anxiety -> questioning whether to have children
exposure_items_quoted: Hogg Eco-anxiety Scale (possible score range: 0 to 39), mean = 13.1, SD = 10.1
outcome: Agreement that climate change makes them question whether they will have children
notes: PREVALENCE, NOT AN ASSOCIATION. This is the single best prevalence estimate available to the chapter -- n=2834 US youth 16-24, published in PNAS -- and TICK-052 needs exactly this quantity: the share of the population holding the dread strongly enough for it to bear on childbearing. But 'questions whether they will have children' is a long way from a birth, and the chapter must not convert it into one. Models adjust for age, sex, education, family affluence, rural/urban and ethnicity -- NOT political orientation.

estimand: climate change beliefs -> ideal number of children
exposure_measure: Climate change belief scales alongside COVID-19 experience
exposure_items_quoted: a series of scales with which to assess their beliefs about climate change
effect_value: the SIGNIFICANT predictor was COVID-19 experience, not climate belief
notes: THE REPORTED SIGNIFICANT RESULT IS NOT THE CLIMATE ONE. Knowing someone hospitalised or dead from COVID-19 predicted a GREATER ideal number of children (Adj R2 = 0.06). The climate-belief coefficient is not the headline and needs extraction from the body. Classified mixed because 'beliefs about climate change' spans risk perception and general belief rather than dread specifically. The COVID comparison is incidentally a mortality-salience benchmark worth noting.

exposure_measure: Exposure to Cyclone Idai and the household instability it caused
exposure_items_quoted: Environmental disruptions such as extreme weather events ... financial, marital, and housing instability
notes: PRECISION-RULE-3 BOUNDARY, SAME CLASS AS THE AEA AIR-POLLUTION STUDY THE RA CHOSE TO KEEP. The exposure is physical (a cyclone) rather than expressed ecological dread, and the mechanism the authors describe is financial, marital and housing instability -- which is C.5.a's mechanism, not D.3.b's. The seam rule keeps it in scope because the OUTCOME is an intention. Retained for consistency with the AEA decision and flagged; if the RA reconsiders that decision, this study moves with it. Note it is also the ONLY sub-Saharan African study in the sample and the only high-fertility setting besides Bangladesh.

estimand: perceptions of climate change -> reproductive intentions
exposure_measure: Perceptions of climate change and attitudes toward death
exposure_items_quoted: Reproductive Intentions Affected by Perceptions of Climate Change and Attitudes toward Death
effect_value: contradicts the legacy hypothesis; only those who already [had children] ...
notes: Reports a CONTRADICTION with the legacy hypothesis (that people leave an environmental legacy for offspring): having children was associated with increased environmental attitudes and behaviours, which is the REVERSE direction. Relevant to the reverse-causality domain in TICK-050 and to the Peters reciprocal design. Coefficients need extraction.

estimand: climate change concern -> intended family size
exposure_measure: Concern about climate change / foreseen unhealthy environment
exposure_items_quoted: individuals fearing for a foreseen unhealthy environment tend to delay or forgo childbearing
effect_value: moderated by EDUCATION: better-educated and worried prefer smaller families than less-educated and worried
notes: THE MODERATOR IS THE D.1.a CONFOUND ITSELF. The climate-concern effect appears among the better educated and not among the less educated, and education is one of the three variables (with political orientation and secularism) that define the Wall 1 boundary. That is exactly the pattern predicted if the association is partly postmaterialist value change rather than dread. VERSION NOTE: retrieved copy is the 2013 VID working paper, not the 2015 Palgrave chapter; coefficients may differ.

exposure_items_quoted: interviews with Australians who are not parents aged 24-35
notes: OFF-POOL, qualitative. Substantive content is adoption and alternative kinship as an ethical response to overpopulation. Narrative evidence for the carbon-ethics cell.

exposure_measure: Interviews with people who have already restricted reproduction for environmental reasons
exposure_items_quoted: 16 participants who have restricted reproduction due to environmental concerns
notes: OFF-POOL, AND SAMPLED ON THE OUTCOME. Participants were recruited BECAUSE they had already restricted reproduction for environmental reasons, so the design cannot speak to prevalence, to effect size, or to whether ecological concern causes the choice. It characterises the reasoning of people who made it. Useful for the mechanism section; must never be counted as evidence of an association.

OFF-POOL, qualitative. I initially suspected this was an OFF_OUTCOME misroute because a keyword sweep found no fertility terms; checking the text showed otherwise -- 'The most profound impact was on reproductive choices, with the majority of participants adamantly rejecting having children.' The routing is correct. Recorded here because the near-miss is the argument for checking text rather than counts.

exposure_items_quoted: Qualitative Auto-Photography Study ... Climate Change, Family Planning, Eco-Anxiety
notes: OFF-POOL, qualitative, and a preprint (Research Square, v2). Narrative evidence only.

estimand: environmental concern -> intention and intended number
exposure_measure: Dichotomous single items; the operative significant predictor is a carbon-ethics item
exposure_items_quoted: childlessness has a positive impact on the environment
outcome: Intention to have children; intended number
effect_value: concerned students still want children but plan fewer
notes: Already extracted at the gate; carried here for completeness. Classified mixed because the only significant environmental predictor in the logistic model is the carbon-ethics item rather than a fear measure.
